newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NZ FAIL TO BUILD ON YOUNG HALF-CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ FAIL TO BUILD ON YOUNG HALF-CENTURY.

text.p: A half-century from opener Bryan Young steered New Zealand to a total of 237 on Wednesday as they fought to save the one-day international cricket series against England.
But Young lacked support from his fellow-batsmen, who once again lost their wickets cheaply after making solid starts.

Nathan Astle skied a catch to wicketkeeper Alec Stewart after hitting seven boundaries in a breezy 34 from 32 balls. Captain Lee Germon, promoted to number three, was stumped off Robert Croft's bowling for 22.
The middle order fell cheaply and England all-rounder Craig White picked up four for 37 as the tourists dismissed New Zealand two balls before the close of their allotted 50 overs.

England recalled White and captain Mike Atherton, who was rested with a back injury in the last match, in place of Allan Mullally and John Crawley, while New Zealand preferred paceman Geoff Allott to spinner Dipak Patel.
New Zealand are fighting to keep the five-match series alive after losing the first two games.
